summary: Champa Thupten Zongtse worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, where he was attested in 1991 and served as a lecturer in 2009.

Chandima Bogahawatta works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Archaeology, and Shandong University. He served as senior lecturer at the University of Kelaniya and professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Chandima Gangodawila, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura. He was a research fellow at the University of Victoria, associate editor at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, and assistant professor at Ateneo de Manila University.

Chandra R. de Silva was a historian and archaeologist. He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991) and as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University (attested 2006).

Chandrabhal Tripathi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen, the University of Cologne, and was a professor at the Free University of Berlin from around 1978 to 1994.

Chandrabhan P. Yadav is a Buddhist studies scholar and historian who completed a PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2021. He served as assistant professor at Indraprastha College for Women and at the National Law School of India University.

Chandradhar Sharma Guleri worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology after studying at the University of Allahabad. He served as Head Pandit at Mayo College (~1904–1920) and held a post at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922).

Chandrika Das works in Tibetology and history/archaeology, pursuing a PhD in History at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi. She held NCWEB guest faculty posts at the University of Delhi and Miranda House.

Chang Huang is a Tibetologist who studied at China University of Geosciences, the University of Wollongong, and the University of Hong Kong. He held postdoctoral positions at the University of Hong Kong and Wageningen University & Research.

Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. He studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and doctoral supervisor Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, Noritoshi Aramaki, and Shoryu Katsura. He served as a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He later held posts at Northwest University, Xiamen University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Peking University (~1934–1948).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Tokyo. His doctoral supervisors included Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda, and he also studied under John D. Dunne.

Channa Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at Leiden University under Jonathan A. Silk. Li held a postdoc at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and a research fellowship at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Chao-heng Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held positions at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene Makley is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Michigan under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She serves as an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Albert Ferguson was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania. He served at the Foreign Service Institute, Harvard University, the Center for Applied Linguistics as director, and was Professor of Linguistics at Stanford University.

Charles Alexander Moore was a philosopher who earned degrees from Yale University. He taught at Yale and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967), and founded and edited the journal Philosophy East and West.
Charles Alfred Bell was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Winchester College and New College, Oxford, and served as a Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society.

Charles Arthur Roe worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Merton College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1863–1898) and was Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University in 1895.
